# ii. Technology Stack {.unnumbered}

## Web Application and Interface

PACS uses **Python 3.11** in its Docker image. The application is split between
two Python web processes:

| Technology | Use in PACS |
|---|---|
| **Flask 3** | Website routes, authentication, site data, model wrapper pages, and report endpoints. |
| **Flask-Login** and **Werkzeug** | User sessions and password hashing. |
| **Jinja, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript** | Server-rendered pages, forms, layout, and browser interactions. |
| **Panel 1.4.5** | Interactive scientific dashboards and editable scenario tables. |
| **Bokeh 3.4.3** | Interactive plots embedded in Flask and Panel pages. |

Panel and Bokeh are pinned to compatible versions. Other runtime packages use
supported version ranges in **requirements.txt**. Developers should install
from that file instead of choosing package versions independently.

## Scientific and Data Libraries

| Technology | Use in PACS |
|---|---|
| **NumPy** and **SciPy** | Numerical arrays, scientific functions, interpolation, integration, and equation solving. |
| **Pandas** | Tabular input, scenario data, CSV processing, and result preparation. |
| **Shapely** and **KDEpy** | Geometry operations and selected statistical analyses. |
| **FloPy** | Creates and runs MODFLOW 6 groundwater flow and transport simulations. |
| **MODFLOW 6.7.0** | Numerical GWF and GWT solver installed in the Docker image. |
| **Matplotlib** | Static scientific plots and images used in reports. |
| **ReportLab** | Branded PDF report generation. |

The numerical runner locates MODFLOW through **MF6_EXE**. Local developers may
also place a platform-specific executable in the ignored **.modflow_bin/**
directory. Solver binaries and generated numerical workspaces must stay out of
Git.

## Database and Deployment

PACS uses **MySQL 8.4** in Docker and connects with
**mysql-connector-python**. **data_queries.py** defines the active runtime
schema. **db_setup.sql** must mirror that schema so a new Compose database is
initialized consistently.

Production-style containers use **Gunicorn** for Flask, **Nginx** as the public
reverse proxy, and **Docker Compose** to coordinate Nginx, Flask, Panel, and
MySQL. Compose health checks prevent Nginx from starting before the application
services are ready. Persistent volumes keep MySQL data and queued numerical job
data across container restarts.

::: {.callout-note appearance=simple icon=false}
**[SC] Figure placeholder: fig8-ii-03.png**

Suggested screenshot: the four services reported as healthy by
**docker compose ps**.

Future location: **contents/develop/images/code-libraries/fig8-ii-03.png**
:::

Development-only packages are listed in **requirements-dev.txt**. It includes
the runtime requirements and adds pytest, keeping production and test
dependencies clearly separated.
